stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed improvement, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality model outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, now integrates MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, significantly boosting local AI inference speed.
The feature is currently available in preview, indicating ongoing development and optimization efforts.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: India's first privately-developed rocket reaches orbit on dramatic debut launch
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: India achieved a significant milestone with the successful orbital launch of its first privately-developed rocket.
The launch represents a major step forward in indigenous space technology development within India.
The success is highlighted by the sentiment of the involved personnel, marking a significant achievement.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat satellites are being deployed to improve wildfire detection capabilities.
The new system is designed to identify wildfires that existing satellite technology often fails to detect.
The deployment is timely, addressing the severe smoke and wildfire issues currently affecting the US and Canada.

stories.title: CRAFT: Clustering Rubrics to Diagnose Weak LLM Capabilities and Generate Targeted Fine-Tuning Data
stories.author: Yunzhong He
bullet_points: Introduces CRAFT, a new method to diagnose the underlying reasons for LLM failures, moving beyond simple performance measurement.
CRAFT converts rubric-based evaluation datasets into specific diagnoses of weak model capabilities.
The tool facilitates the generation of targeted fine-tuning data to improve future model iterations.

stories.title: Harmonizing AI Safety Thresholds
stories.author: Markov Grey
bullet_points: Frontier AI companies use disparate capability thresholds, hindering third-party verification and cross-company comparison.
Lack of common safety thresholds risks inconsistent risk mitigation and a 'race to the bottom' in AI safety standards.
The paper proposes a methodology to derive harmonized safety thresholds across three distinct risk domains (including misuse risks).

stories.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization
stories.author: Sasa Misailovic
bullet_points: Introduces PagedWeight, a novel serving method specifically designed for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs.
Addresses the memory tension in MoE serving between large model weights and growing KV caches.
Achieves efficiency by dynamically quantizing MoE model weights at runtime, balancing precision and cache size.

stories.title: Learning Standard Model structure from LHC data with Riemannian flow matching
stories.author: Oleg Ruchayskiy
bullet_points: Introduces ShellFlow, a Riemannian conditional flow matching model, to learn the Standard Model structure.
The model uses a single transformer-based generative model to cover a vast range of invariant mass (sub-GeV to TeV).
It generates particles directly on their on-shell manifold, leveraging only the on-shell condition as a physics prior.

stories.title: Frontier AI performance across the business disciplines: a case-grounded benchmark of knowledge work and analytical reasoning
stories.author: Mitch Weiss
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation by focusing on real-world knowledge work, rather than just narrow benchmarks.
It proposes a case-grounded benchmark to measure LLM performance in complex tasks like synthesizing information and exercising judgment.
This research highlights that current AI benchmarks fail to adequately test the analytical reasoning required by white-collar professionals.

stories.title: 1-Bit LLM in the Browser
stories.author: simonebrunozzi
bullet_points: Introduction of a 1-Bit Large Language Model (LLM).
The model is designed to run directly within the web browser.
This suggests a major step toward highly efficient, local AI inference.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also introduces web search capabilities to Claude Code.
This enhances the functionality of AI agents by enabling more complex, multi-step tasks and real-time information retrieval.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: A government pilot program is testing the use of Artificial Intelligence in insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the dual potential of AI in prior authorization: fixing inefficiencies or exacerbating existing problems.
This touches upon the intersection of AI deployment, healthcare administration, and regulatory oversight.

stories.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
stories.author: Md Rayhanur Rahman
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) to process security data.
The goal is to transform unstructured threat information (like CVE entries) into structured data.
The application is highly relevant to enhancing cybersecurity for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs).

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the Muon optimizer in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training, comparing it against AdamW.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) framework significantly boosted validation success from 0.290 to 0.546.
The findings suggest Muon offers a substantial performance advantage in sparse-reward RL tasks over standard AdamW controls.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the concept of 'active observation' in human vision, where gaze is continuously redirected based on hypotheses.
It highlights a gap in current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and vision-language benchmarks regarding whether they perform active observation.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to empirically measure active observation capabilities in ML models.

stories.title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
stories.author: Shuiwang Ji
bullet_points: The paper investigates the performance advantages of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) versus Single-Agent Systems (SAS) in LLM-powered complex tasks.
It introduces an Information Bottleneck perspective to theoretically explain the differences between MAS and SAS.
A key finding is that SAS maintains a full reasoning trace in a shared context, whereas MAS utilizes isolated local contexts connected by boundaries.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ToolSciVer, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
Addresses limitations in current methods, specifically struggling with locating decisive visual evidence and interpreting structured scientific visuals.
Utilizes a tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning approach to integrate multimodal observations for reliable scientific reasoning.

stories.title: A Methodology for Auditable Trustworthiness Levels in AI Lifecycle Governance
stories.author: Andrea Ferrario
bullet_points: Addresses the need for continuous, auditable trustworthiness assessment throughout the AI lifecycle.
Fills a gap between high-level AI trustworthiness concepts and practical, lifecycle monitoring.
Proposes a lightweight methodology to make trustworthiness judgments transparent and contestable for governance.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in research between LLM pretraining and subsequent Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
It highlights two open research questions: how pretraining choices influence RL efficiency, and the specific impact of RL on the model's capabilities.
The study aims to overcome the difficulty of analyzing these interactions due to the vast and uncontrolled nature of pretraining data.

stories.title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems
stories.author: Andrea Manzoni
bullet_points: The paper addresses the sample inefficiency of Reinforcement Learning (RL) when applied to complex dynamical systems.
It proposes using physics-enhanced RL to improve the efficiency of synthesizing optimal control strategies.
This approach aims to overcome limitations in RL applications caused by the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional spaces.

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the optimizer 'Muon' in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training, contrasting it with AdamW.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the GiGPO framework significantly boosted validation success from 0.290 to 0.546.
The results suggest Muon offers a substantial performance advantage in this specific RL application, while high-rate AdamW controls showed no improvement.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current benchmarks regarding whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) perform 'active observation,' mimicking human vision.
Active observation, where gaze is continuously redirected based on hypotheses, is presented as a crucial element of human cognition.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to empirically measure the concept of active observation in ML models.

stories.title: PRISA: Proactive Infrastructure LiDAR Framework for Intersection Safety Assessment
stories.author: Hoang H. Nguyen
bullet_points: Introduces PRISA, a new LiDAR framework designed for proactive safety assessment at urban intersections.
The system utilizes privacy-preserving and low-light-robust roadside sensors for continuous traffic monitoring.
Aims to anticipate multi-agent conflicts involving vehicles and vulnerable road users (VRUs) before accidents occur.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current benchmarks regarding whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) perform 'active observation,' a concept rooted in cognitive science.
Active observation posits that human vision is a continuous, hypothesis-driven loop, not a single snapshot.
The authors introduce ActiveVision, a new benchmark designed to empirically measure active observation capabilities in ML models.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ToolSciVer, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
Addresses key challenges in MSCV, such as locating decisive visual evidence and accurately interpreting scientific figures/tables.
Utilizes a tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning approach to integrate multimodal observations for reliable scientific reasoning.

stories.title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels Under Controlled Linguistic Content
stories.author: Desmond Elliott
bullet_points: The research compares three different text encodings (tokens, bytes, and pixels) used in language models.
The study controls for linguistic content and downstream capacity across thirteen languages and five scripts.
It investigates what each encoding preserves when subjected to a shared bottleneck, addressing current modeling limitations.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between LLM pretraining and subsequent Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
It aims to answer how pretraining choices (data, size) influence the effectiveness of RL compute.
The study seeks to elucidate the specific functional impact of RL on the model's capabilities.

stories.title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
stories.author: Kaifeng Lyu
bullet_points: Frontier Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit unexpected failures in simple tasks, specifically exact string copying.
The research attributes this failure to the inductive bias of positional encodings in Transformer architectures.
The models favor local context matching shortcuts over precise positional referencing when attempting to copy text.

stories.title: Loop the Loopies!
stories.author: Bryan Dai
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loopie,' a new series of powerful looped Transformer models.
The models utilize a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, featuring 20B and 6B parameter variants.
Addresses a known limitation in looped Transformers where scaling compute often favors increasing parameter count over looping.

stories.title: Claude found a counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture
stories.author: news.ycombinator.com via jmillikin
bullet_points: Claude (an AI model) reportedly found a counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture.
The Jacobian Conjecture is a significant, long-standing problem in mathematics.
This news suggests advanced AI capabilities in complex mathematical problem-solving.

bullet_points: Focuses on the practical engineering challenge of moving LLM evaluation from subjective assessment ('vibes') to quantifiable metrics.
Addresses the need for robust, production-grade pipelines for LLM quality assurance.
Relevant to ML engineers and MLOps practitioners working with large language models.
